title: Frico Friulano
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A rustic cake of shredded potatoes, onions, and Montasio cheese, pan-fried until the outside turns deeply golden and crisp while the cheese inside stays meltingly soft.
longDesc: Frico comes from Friuli-Venezia Giulia in Italy's northeast corner, where it began as a way to use up aging cheese rinds, and has since evolved into this beloved potato-and-cheese cake, crisp outside and irresistibly gooey within.
ingredients: 600 g (1.3 lb) potatoes, peeled and grated
400 g (14 oz) Montasio cheese (or a mix of aged and young), grated
steps: Squeeze the grated potatoes well to remove excess moisture.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick skillet and sauté the onion until soft and golden.
Add the grated potatoes to the pan with the onion, season, and press down into an even layer.
Cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until the underside is golden and crisp.
Scatter the grated cheese evenly over the potatoes.
Continue cooking until the cheese begins to melt and the bottom is deeply golden, about 5 more minutes.
Carefully flip the frico using a large plate, then slide it back into the pan to crisp the second side.
Cook for another 8–10 minutes until both sides are deeply golden and crisp.
Slide onto a board, let rest for a couple of minutes, then slice into wedges and serve hot.
chefTips: Squeezing as much moisture as possible from the grated potatoes is key to achieving a properly crisp result.
A good non-stick pan makes the flipping process far easier and less risky.
Montasio is traditional, but a mix of any good melting and aged cheeses works well as a substitute.
commonMistakes: Skipping the moisture-squeezing step, resulting in a soggy rather than crisp frico.
Flipping too early, before the bottom has properly set and crisped.
Using only mild, low-flavor cheese, which misses the savory depth good frico depends on.
storage: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days.
reheating: Reheat in a dry skillet to help re-crisp; the microwave will leave it soft and greasy.
healthBenefits: A good source of calcium and protein from the cheese, though rich and best enjoyed occasionally.
culturalNote: Frico is a defining dish of Friuli-Venezia Giulia, historically made by shepherds and farmers as a way to use up cheese scraps, now celebrated as a regional specialty in its own right.
